why: The first rung under packages, asked again now that the seat no longer decides a match. Search 8 (#170) asked it first and named its own tell: the greedy mirror gave Player 1 all 400 benchmark matches, so two deterministic agents that pick alike were decided by who sat first, and a table of scores near 0.5000 would be the seat and not skill. ADR 0063 rolls a tie between the sides on a d20 and lets each side order its own, and the same mirror now gives Player 1 190 of 400 (journal, 2026-09-23): the dice decide it, not the seat. Nothing else moves -- the same panel (greedy, stun-first, random, a candidate ranking last if it falls below the start against any of them), the same check opponent (search-4), the same start (the built-in weights, because whether the old ladder transfers to packages is the question), the same budget and search seed -- so this run and search 8 differ by the rule and nothing else. What would make it a rung: a set that beats stun-first on seeds it never saw. What would make it unreadable now is different: the heuristic agent keeps the order its ties were rolled in, so a weight that only matters through who acts first within a tie cannot show; the lookahead agent orders its own, and a rung for it is a separate search of kind `lookahead`.
